description:
Deterministic, training-calibrated rigid-motion inference from depth–time peak-count rasters.

Core idea
- For each 1 s time bin, z-score the 132-bin depth profile (zero-mean across depth, unit variance).
- For every pair of time bins (i<j), compute the normalized cross-correlation over integer spatial shifts within ±60 μm (±12 bins). The best shift s_ij and its correlation c_ij give a relative displacement measurement: x_j - x_i ≈ s_ij·5 μm.
- Keep only reliable edges with c_ij ≥ 0.1. Weight each edge by (c_ij - 0.1) and a temporal proximity decay exp(-|i-j|/τ).
- Solve a global least-squares problem over all time bins to find displacements x_t that fit the pairwise constraints while being temporally smooth: minimize Σ_e w_e^2(x_j - x_i - d_e)^2 + λ Σ_t (x_t - x_{t-1})^2. A small anchor on x_0 removes the null gauge; the scorer later subtracts the mean per recording.

Training
- Build edges on each of the 4 training recordings (no label leakage).
- Grid-search τ ∈ {8,12,18,30,45,60} s and λ ∈ {0.001,0.003,0.01,0.03,0.1,0.3,1,3}; for each pair, solve all 4 recordings and select the combination minimizing average RMSE versus mean-removed train_y.

Prediction
- For each test recording, rebuild edges from its raster only (no cross-record borrowing) and solve once with the trained (τ,λ). Return the raw x (any constant offset is allowed; scorer mean-centers).

Computational notes
- Depth-bin size is 5 μm, so shifts are integer bins. Normalized cross-correlations are computed per pair with proper overlap normalization and a minimal overlap of 40 bins to stabilize scores.
- The global system is solved via a dense 90×90 linear system (normal equations). λ is scaled by the ratio trace(M)/trace(L) for stability across recordings.
- Deterministic, no randomized operations. Uses only NumPy and math. Fits the 180 s/1-thread/4 GB constraints comfortably.
